solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ban on singing in theatre momentarily retracted

indicators.note: retracted says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A stage show is briefly barred from including songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singing' is slang for informing to the police, not performing music.
explanation.definitionFit: Omertà is the Mafia code of silence, a prohibition on informing to the authorities.

clue.text: Expose one swapping partners in kind of ball

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them
a swinger is someone who swaps sexual partners

explanation.surface: A newspaper exposes a wife-swapper at some kind of dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball' suggests a dance; it is a cricket delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an outswinger is a delivery that curves away from the batsman through the air.

clue.text: Fears removing outer layer will reveal slip

indicators.note: removing the outer layer strips away the first and last letters

parts.note: terrors are fears

explanation.surface: Fears that peeling away a surface will expose a slip, like underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake, which is what an error is.

clue.text: Perhaps patients without pressure, which prevents any issue

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the phrase goes round the letter

parts.note: patients are an example of the ill
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Patients who are not under pressure, perhaps, avoid problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking. 'Issue' means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: The contraceptive pill prevents pregnancy, and issue is an old word for children.

clue.text: Consider cut in part of book

indicators.note: in says the word for cut is placed within the part of the book

parts.note: the cover is the outside part of a book
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: An editor weighs up trimming a chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: To chew something over is an idiom for thinking it through at length.

clue.text: Event for women with 50 per cent reduction on a beauty product

indicators.note: a fifty per cent cut keeps only the first half of the phrase

parts.note: a hen night is a party for a bride-to-be and her female friends

explanation.surface: A sale on a cosmetic at a women's event.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen night is the British name for a bachelorette party; its first half is HENN.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish plant dye used on hair and to decorate skin, a cosmetic.

clue.text: Current rabbit cages providing more amusement

indicators.note: cages means the outer word encloses the other

parts.note: to rabbit (on) is British slang for chatter, as is to witter
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A rabbit in a hutch these days is more fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' is a verb, British slang for talking on and on, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wittier means more clever and funny, so more entertaining.

clue.text: Lapse from this person in grasping maths ratio

indicators.note: in places the letter for this person within the word for grasping

parts.note: venal means greedy or corruptible, grasping
this person, the setter, is I
sin is short for sine, a trigonometric ratio

explanation.surface: A slip-up made by me, while getting to grips with a mathematical ratio.
explanation.definitionFit: A venial sin is a minor, pardonable wrong, a moral lapse rather than a grave offence.

clue.text: Speaker's set down mnemonic method

indicators.note: a speaker says it out loud, signalling a soundalike

parts.note: to set down in writing is to write, so wrote

explanation.surface: The Speaker of the House has laid down a memory technique.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning by rote means memorising through repetition, a technique for remembering.

clue.text: In South Dakota, person devoid of charms ran

indicators.note: In at the start says the person goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota
in Harry Potter a Muggle is a person with no magic, so no spells or charms

explanation.surface: An unattractive person ran off in South Dakota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charms' suggests good looks, but it means magic spells.
explanation.definitionFit: To run goods, such as guns or drugs, is to smuggle them.

clue.text: He may be on the end of a cross termagant's raving

definitions.text: He may be on the end of a cross

indicators.note: raving suggests wild disorder, so the letters of termagant are jumbled

explanation.surface: An angry, scolding woman is ranting at someone cross.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'cross' is a football pass from the wing into the box, not an angry person.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a target man is a tall forward whom teammates aim crosses and long balls at.

clue.text: Maxim or Henry quitting information superhighway

indicators.note: quitting says the unit letter leaves the phrase for the online world

parts.note: the information superhighway is an old name for the internet, the Net
H is the symbol for the henry, the SI unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone called Maxim, or one called Henry, is leaving the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maxim or Henry' reads like a pair of names; Maxim is the definition and 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held as true, much like a maxim or guiding rule.

clue.text: What many commuters do to secure good ready money

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the outer phrase grips the letter for good

parts.note: commuters travel in to work in the capital city

explanation.surface: Commuters slog into town to earn decent cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Working capital is the liquid funds a business has available for day-to-day operations, i.e. cash to hand.

clue.text: Striking hard criminal using harsh language

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
cussing is swearing

explanation.surface: A violent crook swears as they hit out.
explanation.definitionFit: To concuss is to strike violently, as a heavy blow to the head does.

clue.text: Chemist Boots' opening during festival

indicators.note: during places the opening letter inside the festival word

parts.note: Noel is Christmas, a festival

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of Boots'

explanation.surface: A branch of the Boots pharmacy chain opens during a festive period.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is a British high-street pharmacy chain, which is why 'Chemist' reads as a shop; here it is a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel, founder of the Nobel Prizes, was a Swedish chemist who invented dynamite.

clue.text: Polish up drafts for either of two US novelists

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to polish is to rub
roughs are rough drafts or sketches

explanation.surface: Revising early drafts, as a novelist would.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgar Rice Burroughs wrote Tarzan; William S. Burroughs wrote Naked Lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Two American novelists share this surname, so either one fits the clue.

clue.text: Italian red meat course nearly cooked

parts.note: lamb is a meat

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are worked over into a new order
nearly means the last letter of the word is left off

parts.note: a course of a meal, taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: A meat dish at an Italian meal that is not quite done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims COURSE to COURS, and 'cooked' rearranges that into RUSCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambrusco is a sparkling red wine from the Emilia-Romagna region of Italy.

clue.text: One getting wind about bad hearing

indicators.note: about means the wind word goes around the letter for one

parts.note: the mistral is a cold north wind of southern France
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone caught in a gale has trouble hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' is a court hearing, not the sense of sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistrial is a trial rendered invalid by error, a flawed court hearing.

clue.text: Poor side in Peru wanting new playmaker

indicators.note: poor suggests a bad state, so the letters are rearranged
wanting means lacking, so a letter is taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: A weak Peruvian team lacks a creative midfielder.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of SIDE IN PERU minus N, from 'wanting new', rearrange to the answer. 'Playmaker' suggests football but means a writer of plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Euripides was one of the great tragic dramatists of ancient Athens, a maker of plays.

clue.text: Small cake or a little fish?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small thick pancake or crumpet
second meaning, playful: a young pike, with -let meaning small

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense is invented: pike plus the diminutive ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A pikelet is a British and Australian griddle cake, and read cryptically, a small pike.

clue.text: Like a party hat or fleece coat from Isaac

parts.note: to fleece is to swindle, or con

indicators.note: the coat of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A party hat, or a fleece jacket belonging to Isaac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link word between the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A party hat is typically cone-shaped, and conic means shaped like a cone.

clue.text: Cover up in fancy lace — it's seen in façade

indicators.note: in places the reversed cover inside the rearranged lace
fancy suggests something elaborate, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: Hiding something beneath ornate lace on the front of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a picture: the mark under the c of façade is the thing being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A cedilla is the hook beneath the c in façade, a diacritic mark.

clue.text: Royal house engaged in retail in scenic area

parts.note: York was an English royal house, as in the Wars of the Roses

indicators.note: in places the word for engaged inside the word for retail

parts.note: retail is the business of sales
engaged as in taken on, hired

explanation.surface: A member of the royal family has taken a job in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yorkshire Dales are an upland national park in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yorkshire Dales are a famously beautiful region of valleys and moorland, a scenic area.

clue.text: Taking things quickly, takes repast briefly

parts.note: to have is to take, as in have a meal

indicators.note: briefly cuts the final letter off the word

parts.note: tea is a meal, a repast

explanation.surface: Someone eats lunch in a rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is speed or hurry in doing things.

clue.text: Sozzled after leaving bachelor's house

indicators.note: after leaving means a letter has gone out of the word

parts.note: sozzled and blotto are both slang for very drunk

explanation.surface: Drunk after quitting a single man's home.
explanation.walkthrough: House, or housey-housey, is an old British name for bingo.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of numbers drawn at random, the same as bingo, once called house.

clue.text: I see Jack is one with Jezebel for a partner

definitions.text: one with Jezebel for a partner

parts.note: ah! is an exclamation of realisation, like I see
a jack is a sailor, as is an AB, able seaman

explanation.surface: Someone realises that Jack is the man paired with Jezebel.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, King Ahab of Israel married the notorious queen Jezebel.

clue.text: One who philosophised on what comes from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means read right to left

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
eh? is an exclamation meaning what?

explanation.surface: A thinker muses about things arriving from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Hegel was a German philosopher, central to nineteenth-century idealism.

clue.text: Opera pioneer — he abandons affected theatricals

indicators.note: affected suggests something altered or put on, so the letters are rearranged
abandons means the letters of he leave the pool

explanation.surface: An opera pioneer walks away from pretentious stage antics.
explanation.walkthrough: THEATRICALS less H and E, from 'he abandons', rearranges to the composer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alessandro Scarlatti was a Baroque composer regarded as a founder of the Neapolitan school of opera.

clue.text: Conquered hiding place where Daniel is taken

indicators.note: hiding says the outer word conceals the other piece inside it

parts.note: to best someone is to beat them, so bested means conquered
the Book of Daniel is in the Old Testament, OT

explanation.surface: Someone defeated holes up where Daniel was held, the lions' den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conquered' wants to be the definition, but it is BESTED; the definition is 'taken', as in smitten.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken with someone is to be charmed by them, and besotted means infatuated.

clue.text: Wrap-around garment's grand and not equally twisted

indicators.note: twisted says the run of pieces is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
nor means and not
as, as in as tall, means equally

explanation.surface: A wrap-around item of clothing is impressive and also unevenly wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarong is a length of cloth wound around the waist, worn in South and Southeast Asia.
